draft.title: SWOT analysis
card: A SWOT analysis is a list that helps a business plan. It sorts what affects the business into four groups: strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats.
These are internal. They come from inside the business, so the business can control them. Examples are skilled staff or old equipment.
These are external. They come from outside the business, so the business cannot control them. Examples are a new road past the shop or a new competitor.
The business then plans to use its strengths, fix its weaknesses, take up opportunities and prepare for threats.
draft.remember: SWOT sorts what a business can control (inside) from what it cannot (outside).

a.q: Which of these is an internal weakness of a business?
opts: Its delivery van is old and often breaks down
A new competitor opens in the same street
The council plans to build a new bus stop nearby
Customers in the area are starting to prefer online shopping
a.why: The van belongs to the business, so the problem is internal and the business can fix it. The competitor is a threat from outside, so it is external and not a weakness.
a.clue: Which problem sits inside the business itself?

b.q: Mia runs a café in Dubbo. A large mining company opens a new site nearby and hundreds of workers move to town. In her SWOT analysis, where does this belong?
opts: Opportunity, because it is external and may bring customers
Strength, because it may bring customers to her café
Threat, because it is external and she cannot control it
Weakness, because she did not plan for it
b.why: The mine is outside the café and Mia cannot control it, so it is external. It may bring more customers, so it is an opportunity. It is not a strength, because strengths come from inside the business.
b.clue: First ask if Mia controls it, then ask if it helps her.

a.best: Its delivery van is old and often breaks down

b.best: Opportunity, because it is external and may bring customers
